topology_analysis.structure: Elliptical ring resonator with two symmetric loading pads
topology_analysis.description: This device consists of (1) an elliptical outer ring (black material), (2) two rectangular coupling pads positioned symmetrically above and below the ring's centerline, (3) each pad contains two window cutouts (white) separated by a divider bar, (4) arms connect the pads to the ring.
topology_analysis.function: Ring resonator with symmetric coupling/loading structure. The pads couple power in/out of the ring cavity. The windows and divider create interference nodes for wavelength-selective coupling.
key_components: Ring material: thickness defines cavity Q
Top pad: rectangular frame above center, contains 2 windows + divider
Bottom pad: mirror of top pad
Tapered arms: connect pads to ring perimeter
function_knobs: pad_width: horizontal size of coupling pads
pad_height: vertical size of coupling pads
window_width: width of each cutout (coupling strength)
divider_width: width of bar separating windows
pad_offset_y: vertical distance of pads from center
arm_flare_width: width at ring connection point

iterations.change_made: Initial build with sonnet's iter-3 params using path.extrude() for ring, boolean subtraction for pads, tapered arms
Increased ring size (ax: 1.35->1.40, ay: 2.70->2.75) - REGRESSION, reverted
Reduced pad size (width: 1.00->0.95, height: 1.17->1.15) - REGRESSION, reverted

final.final_params: ring_ax=1.35, ring_ay=2.70, ring_width=0.34, pad_width=1.00, pad_height=1.17, pad_border=0.22, pad_offset_y=0.91, window_width=0.30, window_height=0.54, divider_width=0.11, arm_width=0.44, arm_flare_width=1.05, arm_length=0.90
final.note: 5-iteration optimization achieving 0.5572 IoU (0.5557 baseline from sonnet iter-3). Improvements made by tuning arm geometry (length +0.05um, flare_width +0.05um). The device is an elliptical ring resonator with two symmetric coupling pads, each containing two window cutouts connected by a divider bar, and tapered arms feeding the ring. All function knobs are top-level assignments in device.py and drive real geometry changes via GDSFactory path.extrude() and taper() primitives.
